name: Plant-watering robot
summary: 1 litre tank, 5 V pump, capacitive soil sensor and an ESP32 on one 18650; runs about a month, stable with a full tank.

spec.name: Windowsill Plant-Watering Robot
spec.function: Waters one potted plant from a 1 litre tank. A small submersible pump sits in the tank and pushes water through a tube into the pot when a capacitive soil moisture sensor reports dry soil. A microcontroller deep-sleeps almost all the time so one 18650 cell lasts a month or more.
spec.quote: Design a plant-watering robot for one pot on my windowsill: a 1 litre water tank, a small pump and a soil moisture sensor. It should run at least a month on its battery, not tip over with a full tank, and cost under 40 euros.

parts.name: Base housing
parts.description: Flat rectangular electronics housing 140 x 140 x 30 mm, centred on X=Y=0, standing on Z=0 (Z 0 to 30). Open box with 2.5 mm walls and 3 mm floor, closed at the top by a 3 mm top plate (Z 27 to 30) with a 110 x 110 mm recess 1 mm deep for the tank, an 8 mm hole at X=0, Y=0 through the plate for the tank outlet, a 6 mm tube hole in the front wall (-Y) at X=-40, Z=15, and a 6 x 3 mm cable slot at the top front edge. Hollow inside for pump, battery and board.

parts.name: Water tank
parts.description: Watertight open-top rectangular water tank, outer 110 x 110 x 100 mm, centred on X=Y=0, standing on the base top (Z 30 to 130). Walls 2 mm, floor 2 mm solid with NO holes anywhere below the rim, inside 106 x 106 x 98 mm. The whole top is the open fill opening. A 10 x 5 mm U-shaped notch in the top of the front wall (-Y) at X=-40, from Z=125 to 130, so the pump tube and cable can leave the tank over the rim. Rounded 3 mm inner vertical corners.

parts.name: Sensor arm
parts.description: Flat horizontal bracket that holds the soil sensor over the pot. A bar 16 mm wide (X from -8 to 8), 6 mm thick (Z 124 to 130), running from Y=-45 (overlapping the front tank wall, with two 3 mm screw holes there) to Y=-150 towards the front. At Y=-145 it has a 24 x 5 mm slot through the bar where the sensor blade is pushed through and held with friction.

parts.name: Soil moisture sensor
parts.description: Capacitive blade sensor, hangs in the soil

parts.name: Controller board
parts.query: ESP32 low power deep sleep board

parts.name: 18650 cell
parts.description: One cell laid flat in the holder

parts.name: 18650 holder with charger and 5 V boost
parts.description: Holds the cell, charges over USB-C, gives 5 V

parts.name: Silicone tubing
parts.description: Tube from the pump over the tank rim to the pot

parts.name: MOSFET pump switch
parts.description: Switches the pump from a controller pin

requirements.text: Runs at least 30 days on one battery charge
requirements.quote: run at least a month on its battery

requirements.text: Tip angle at least 25 degrees with the full 1 litre tank
requirements.quote: not tip over with a full tank

requirements.text: Settles within 5 degrees after a 1 N push at the top with a full tank
requirements.quote: not tip over with a full tank

requirements.text: Sensor arm bends less than 2 mm under the sensor weight

pump.reason: Cheapest 5 V submersible pump, 1.5 l/min is plenty for one pot.

mcu.reason: Deep sleep 0.5 mW, can also send Wi-Fi alerts.

battery.reason: 3000 mAh at 5.9 euros is the cheapest capacity for a month.

holder.reason: Holder, USB-C charging and 5 V boost for pump and board in one part.

tubing.reason: Fits the pump outlet, food safe.

driver.reason: Switches the pump from a 3.3 V pin.
